newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: New chief prosecutor named in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: New chief prosecutor named in Colombia.

text.p: Colombia's Supreme Court named a new chief prosecutor on Thursday to replace Alfonso Valdivieso, the popular anti-drug and corruption fighter who stepped down this month to run for president.

Alfonso Gomez Mendez, a 47-year-old former attorney general with extensive experience in penal law and the judiciary, was the third man to be appointed to the high-profile job of Prosecutor-General since the post was created under Colombia's new constitution in 1992.

The court voted for Gomez by an overwhelming 16-3 majority from a list of three candidates submitted by President Ernesto Samper after Valdivieso resigned on May 8. He is to be sworn in by Samper within about two weeks, taking over what has often been described as Colombia's second most important job as its top lawman.

As chief prosecutor, Valdivieso saw all of Colombia's billionaire cocaine barons jailed or killed and spearheaded an independent probe of Samper's election campaign that nearly led to the president's ouster on drug-corruption charges.

In an interview with Colombian radio, Gomez vowed to carry out his new responsibilities with "absolute independence" and said this would include pursuing the so-called 8,000 Process -- the probe into the campaign finance scandal.
He said he had served as legal counsel to one of Samper's cabinet officials, former Foreign Minister Rodrigo Pardo, when he was accused of covering up the scandal last year.

In brief remarks on Gomez's appointment, Samper said his priority should be an all-out fight against impunity in Colombia, a country where government officials say more than 90 percent of all crimes go unpunished.
